The '''Ocean''' is a [[Biomes|biome]] made up of, much like examples in real life, a vast body of water. It is only realistically accessible by [[boats]], as swimming out from the safety of the shore quickly depletes [[stamina]] and leads to drowning. In many ways, the Ocean acts as less its own dedicated biome, per se, and more a vehicle for player exploration.

Currently the biome only features the elusive and destructive [[Serpent]] enemy as well as the even more elusive [[Leviathan]], a hulking shelled creature covered in shrubbery, algae, and barnacles. These two creatures are the sole way for players to gather [[Serpent Scale|Serpent scales]] and [[Chitin]], respectively.

== Notes ==

* Creatures killed and boats destroyed in the water cause some of the flotsam to sink beneath the waves. A ship being sunk at sea often means heavier objects are lost to the briny deep.
** Examples of floating material include wood and some trophies; nails, pelts, coins, etc. sink to the bottom and can become unreachable. Player deaths in the Ocean biome generate a floating headstone, while a vessel's cargo contents are stored in crates that float above the water.
* There is a simulation of low and high tide within the game on all coast and shore lines.

'''Abyssal Barnacles''' are a [[Materials List|resource]] node and can be mined with a [[Pickaxes (Skill)|pickaxe]] from the backs of [[Leviathan]]s found in the [[Ocean]] biome.

== Availability ==
Each mined barnacle has a 10% chance to trigger the Leviathan's retreat, signaled by a howl sound. Make sure to have a nearby [[Boats|boat]] or land to fall back to when it begins to sink.

== Notes ==
* Any type of pickaxe can be used to mine the barnacles, but higher grade ones are recommended as they will allow for more material to be mined.
* As [[Chitin]] is primarily obtained from barnacles, the only way to obtain additional Chitin after all of a world's Leviathans have been mined for it is by [[Fishing]] using [[Heavy Fishing Bait]]. Chitin can be endlessly obtained this way, although the required bait can be difficult to obtain.

'''Leviathans''' are passive [[creatures]] found in [[Ocean|Oceans]]. They are massive rock-type beings that have a 10% chance of submerging each time their [[Abyssal Barnacle]]s are damaged.

Leviathans themselves are immovable and indestructible; only the barnacles on their back can be destroyed by mining them.

It is not possible to build on Leviathans. 

===Drops===
Each [[Abyssal Barnacle]] drops the following when mined:
{{drop table|
{{drop row|item=Chitin| 0star=3-4}}
|stars=0}}
See their [[Abyssal Barnacle|main page]] for details on how to mine the barnacles.

Each time a barnacle is hit, there is a 10% chance that the leviathan will be disturbed (indicated by it shaking and emitting noise). Once 20 seconds have passed after it is first disturbed, it will begin permanently submerging into the ocean (accompanied by much more shaking and noises). During those 20 seconds, further hits still have a 10% chance to trigger additional shaking.

It takes roughly 25 seconds from the start of the leviathan's submersion process until its entire body is below the waterline. During the first few seconds it actually raises its body up higher, then slowly begins accelerating downward, eventually moving faster than 1 m/s.

=== Spawning===
Leviathans are spawned upon world generation and do not respawn once they have retreated below the depths of the ocean.

They have 1% chance of appearing on each full Ocean [[Spawn zones|zone]] and require at least 30 meters depth.

* As [[Chitin]] is primarily obtained from their barnacles, the only way to obtain additional Chitin after all of a world's Leviathans have been mined for it is by [[Fishing]] using [[Heavy fishing bait]]. Chitin can be endlessly obtained this way, although the required bait can be difficult to obtain.
* To cheese the Leviathan, you can simply log out when it starts sinking. When you log back in, the Leviathan is no longer sinking. This is the only known way to fully mine a Leviathan.

== Trivia ==
* The Leviathan in Valheim is based on the [[wikipedia:Hafgufa|Hafgufa]] from Norse Mythology, and the game is faithful to their original appearance as a large creature that was mistaken for an island. The island is only its shell while the rest of the Hafgufa resides below.
* The ''actual'' [[wikipedia:Leviathan|Leviathan]] is more akin to Valheim's [[Serpent]].
* During [[Day and Night Cycle|night time]], its two glowing eyes can be seen underwater.
* Their underside lacks any distinct features and detail. This is likely intended from a development standpoint because players are only supposed to see the top part of them that is visible above water.

[[Creatures]] use their senses to detect and find enemies (usually players). These senses include seeing and hearing. Creatures cannot smell, so [[wind]] does not affect sensing.

Creatures select the closest enemy as their target that they can see or hear. However, hearing never makes creatures alerted.

== Sight ==
Creatures have the following properties related to sight:

* View range: Distance to see enemies.
* View angle: Field of view. Alerted creatures have full field of view and can see behind their backs.
* Alert range: Distance to get alerted when seeing enemies.
* Eye position: Position of eyes in the character model. Used to check line of sight.

Creatures can see enemies when there is a line of sight from the creature's eyes to the enemy's eyes and the enemy is within the view angle and range.

Stealth reduces a creature's alert and view range based on the visibility bar. For crouching players, the line of sight check uses player center position instead of eye position.

=== Creature properties: ===
Most creatures can see 30 meters away with a 90-degree angle. Most creatures get alerted when seeing a target 20 meters away. Exceptions are listed below:

* [[Lox]]: 15 sight and 6 alert
* [[Boar]], [[Neck]]: 20 sight and 6 alert
* [[Deer]]: 25 sight and 25 alert
* [[Draugr]], [[Draugr Elite]]: 10 alert
* [[Leech]]: 360-degree angle
* [[Blob]], [[Oozer]], [[Yagluth]]: 30 alert
* [[Drake]], [[Wraith]]: 40 sight and 30 alert
* [[Eikthyr]]: 40 sight and 40 alert
* [[Serpent]]: 50 sight, 360-degree angle and 20 alert
* [[Bonemass]]: 50 sight, 80-degree angle and 50 alert
* [[The Elder]]: 50 sight and 50 alert
* [[Moder]]: 60 sight and 60 alert

== Noise ==
Noise is measured as how far away it can be heard. For example, a player that creates 40 noise will attract creatures from 40 meters away. Noise does not stack, instead the highest value is used. Noise decays four per second and usually follows the creature or player that created it.

Players cannot detect noise as it is not related to in-game sounds.

=== Sources of noise ===
* Chopping a tree or mining a resource: Creates 100 noise for the closest player within 10 meters (even when caused by a creature).
* Building, repairing or deconstructing: Creates 50 noise
* Jumping or running: Creates 30 noise (creatures run when alerted)
* Moving or swimming: Creates 15 noise
* Dodging: Creates 5 noise
* Sneaking: Creates 0 noise

Attacking also creates noise depending on the weapon, type of attack and whether something was hit. Noise created by arrows and thrown spears will originate from the hit location but sets the player as the target. Other attacks will originate from the player.

=== Creature properties ===
Creatures have a maximum hearing range that determines how far away they can detect sources of noise. Most creatures have a hearing range of 9999 meters, which is practically infinite. Exceptions are listed below:

For example, a Lox cannot hear a player running or chopping wood from 20 meters away, even though the created noise would reach it.

== Sleeping ==
Sleeping creatures lie on the ground and have reduced senses. They wake up when:

* Receiving damage.
* A player gets within X meters. This is not affected by sneaking, line of sight or noise.
* A player is heard within Y meters.

Noise from arrows and other projectiles will not wake up sleeping creatures, but will make them alerted (which prevents backstabbing).

The following creatures are initially sleeping:
* [[Abomination]]: Wakes up when there is a player within 20 meters. Checked every 0–8 seconds (randomly determined when the creature is loaded).
* [[Ulv]]: Wakes up when there is a player within four meters or when hearing a player within 10 meters. Checked every 0.5 seconds.
* [[Stone Golem]]: Wakes up when there is a player within two meters or when hearing a player within 50 meters. Checked every 0.5 seconds.

'''Stagger''' is a combat state that stuns the target and causes non-player [[creatures]] to take double damage. Stagger is caused in two cases: *The total amount of staggering reaches the stagger limit. *An attack is successfully parried by a player. The stagger duration is different for each creature ranging from near instant to a few seconds. The duration may also be different when parrying certain attacks. While a non-player creature is staggered, every hit against it deals double damage. A new stagger is ignored while the target is already staggered. When a player staggers a creature through damage, the player gains 3 [[Adrenaline|adrenaline]] (multiplied by the creature's adrenaline multiplier). ===Staggering=== Staggering is inflicted when receiving physical (blunt, slash and pierce) and lightning [[damage types]], and the amount of stagger applied is equivalent to the amount of damage taken after resistances and armor, multiplied by the attack's stagger multiplier. Some status effects modify the amount of staggering received. Currently only [[Fader]]'s [[Forsaken power]] does so, halving it. Players also receive extra staggering when blocking based on how much physical or lightning damage got through the block. Staggering gradually expires 20% of the stagger limit per second. Staggering won't be reset when the stagger limit is reached. Staggering won't exceed the stagger limit. The stagger limit is a percentage of the maximum health which generally makes stronger creatures harder to stagger. Creatures with a limit of 0% are immune to stagger from damage. Players with health based [[food]] will have an increased stagger limit which also means that the staggering expires faster. === Increased staggering === Some player attacks cause increased staggering: *1.5x: Two-handed [[Axes|axe]] primary attacks. *2x: Mace secondary attack. This equates to 5x the weapon's listed damage, since the special attack has a 2.5x damage multiplier. *2x: [[Clubs|Sledge]] primary attacks, except the [[Stagbreaker]]. *4x: Two-handed [[Axes|axe]] secondary attack. This equates to 2x the weapon's listed damage, since the special attack has a 0.5x damage multiplier. *6x: Atgeir secondary attack. This equates to 6x the weapon's listed damage, since the special attack has a 1x damage multiplier. *6x: [[Fists]] secondary attack. This equates to 6x the weapon's listed damage, since the special attack has a 1x damage multiplier. === Notes === * Stagger doesn't stack. If the target is already staggered, the new stagger is ignored. This makes faster attacks better at stun-locking targets. * Parrying an attack causes an instant stagger without contributing towards the stagger limit. However the double damage from the stagger helps reaching the limit more easily. ** Only creatures that can be staggered by blocking are affected. [[Bonemass]], [[Moder]], [[The Elder]], [[Yagluth]], [[The Queen]], [[Fader]], [[Kall Fimbulbringer]] and the [[Gammeltroll]] are not staggered by parries. * While blocking causes extra staggering, it also often significantly reduces the damage taken (which reduces staggering). ** If block armor is less than gear armor, then blocking will always increase the total amount of received staggering. * Getting staggered from blocking will cancel the block (but resistances and gear armor will still work). ** However getting staggered from the actual damage taken when blocking won't cancel the block. ==Creature stats== Stagger is based on animations so the duration is affected by animation transitions and animation speed scaling. For example staggering running creatures may result in slightly different stagger duration. Players will also stagger longer if staggered at the right moment when using the sword secondary attack (even up to 5.8 seconds). Duration values seem to vary a few milliseconds because of the animation system. However this won't have an impact on the actual gameplay. === Scratch ===
Swipes at the player with one of its claws (100 [[Damage types#Slash|Slash]] damage). This attack has two variations, each with its own 3-second cooldown: one with the left claw and one with the right. Both variations swing in a 3-meter 115-degree horizontal arc and can be used when within 1.6 meters of a player.

=== Throw ===
Picks up a stone from the ground and lobs it at the player (75 [[Damage types#Pierce|Pierce]] damage). The stone travels at a random velocity between 50–60 meters per second, with a spread of 4–20 degrees. It can travel for up to 4 seconds before despawning. This attack can be used every 6 seconds when between 6–40 meters of a player.

{{Infobox location | title = Mörkhalla | image = Mörkhalla.png | type = Dungeon | id = MorkBorg | location = [[Deep North]] | number = 40 | resources = * [[Memorial Coal]] * [[Moulds]] | inhabitants = * [[Hexen]] * [[Krigen]] * [[Hexahedric Pulp]] * [[Shapeless Pulp]] * [[Tiny Pulp]] * [[Captive Fuling]] * [[Imprisoned Dvergr]] }} '''Mörkhalla''' is a [[dungeon]] found in the [[Deep North]]. An [[Intricate Key]] is required to open its entrance, the Gates of Mörkhalla. The key is not consumed, and the gates can be closed again. Up to 40 Mörkhalla entrances are placed in each world. They can appear anywhere in the Deep North, including near its edges, at an altitude of at least 30 meters, and at least 275 meters apart. ==Description== The dungeon consists of around 14 floors, separated by a large central gap that splits the floors into two separate sides. The two sides can be crossed with various bridges and drawbridges. The entrance is near the top of the dungeon and the most valuable loot can be found on the bottom floor. The dungeon is generated from four or five large sections. Inside, the environment is always dark and counts as [[Cold Effect|cold]], but not freezing. Some gates inside the dungeon, also named Gates of Mörkhalla, consume an Intricate Key when opened and cannot be closed afterwards. ==Resources== All floors are protected by [[Krigen]], [[Hexen]], [[Captive Fuling]], [[Imprisoned Dvergr]] and [[Hexahedric Pulp]]. Captive Fulings and Imprisoned Dvergr spawn when a player comes within 60 meters of their spawn point, with up to two stars. A Hexahedric Pulp has 600 health and spawns a [[Shapeless Pulp]] every 5 seconds while a player is within 20 meters, as long as no other Shapeless Pulp it spawned is nearby. When destroyed, it drops two to three items from {{Item link|Scrap Iron}}, {{Item link|Timberwood}}, {{Item link|Lingonberries}} and {{Item link|Dead Pulp}}. Valuables [[Grimvarn]], [[Solryth]], [[Veydris]] and [[Draumyx]] can be found on the floor or in decorative wall sockets. Some sockets hold {{Item link|Iolite}}, {{Item link|Jade}} or {{Item link|Bloodstone}} instead. Rubble piles can be destroyed for one to five [[Ancient Coin]]s and [[Grausten]]. Piles of wooden debris drop two to three {{Item link|Wood}}. Fire Pits can be destroyed for 2 to 4 [[Memorial Coal]]s or [[Coal]]s. Furniture can be destroyed for [[Timberwood]] and [[Chain]]s. Banners and rugs drop {{Item link|Red Jute}}. Two type of treasure chest, some of them are hidden behind cobweb under stairs: * Ancient Chest: {{Chest|Ancient Chest}} * Jotun's Chest: {{Chest|Jotun's Chest}} ===Bottom floor=== Destroying the [[Malicious Ice]] on the bottom floor immediately starts a [[Jotun Invasion]] event somewhere in the world. The Malicious Ice has 1,000 health. While a player is within 120 meters, it spawns a Krigen or Hexen every 50 seconds, until six of them are within 50 meters. Three in four are Krigen, and they can have up to two stars. Training dummies can be destroyed for Timberwood, [[Barley]] and [[Flax]]. Weapon stands can be destroyed for Timberwood, [[Scrap Iron]], and weapon, staff or shield [[Mould]]s. Coal piles can be destroyed for three to five Memorial Coal. Rolled sleeping spots can be destroyed for [[Asksvin Hide]], [[Moose Hide]], [[Lox Pelt]], and [[Wolf Pelt]]. ==Strategy== The player can jump down the central gap to access the bottom floor quickly and ascend back to the entrance with a [[Grappling Hook]]. The fall can be survived by either wearing the [[Feather Cape]] or having over 100 health (since falling can only deal up to 100 damage). == Lore == [[Munin]] describes the inhabitants of Mörkhalla as a whole, without naming them: "Kraa! Strange folk dwell here, created from the very evil itself..."In-game text, Munin ($npc_munin_deepnorth_morkborg). == Notes == * [[Campfire]]s and [[Cooking Station]]s can be placed inside. * Morkhalla dungeons always have at least one route back to the surface that doesn't require a [[Grappling Hook]] so that players can't get trapped inside it. == References == {{WorldNav}}

They speak when approached, akin to [[Dvergr (race)|Dvergr]]. Shadows never attack, and other creatures ignore them. The furniture can be destroyed for various resources from previous biomes. The trophies on the wall have a 5.5% chance to drop when destroyed. ==Location== Up to 135 village sites (NorthVillage) and 40 Great Halls (thehole01) are placed in each world. Both are only placed away from the edges of the Deep North, at least two meters above sea level. Great Halls are at least 256 meters apart. Each village site is placed within 85 meters of a Great Hall or of another village site, and at least 70 meters from other village sites, so the sites form clusters around the Great Halls. ==Layout== A village consists of 15 to 20 buildings, scattered within a circle of 28 to 30 meters radius and surrounded by a perimeter of eight sections. Buildings are only placed on ground with a slope of at most 25 degrees, and never overlap. Deep North Chests act as beacons with a range of 30 meters, which the [[Wishbone]] can detect. ==Great Hall== [[File:DN Great Hall.png|thumb|left|Great Hall]] Great Halls contain entrances to the [[Winding Tunnels]]. Each Great Hall has four spawn points that each spawn one [[Shadow]], with up to two stars, when a player comes within 60 meters.
